examples: I like their new album.
This album is great.
I listen to the album.
The band has a new album.
She has a talent for music.
He has a real talent for drawing.
Our school has a talent show every spring.
Cooking is not my talent.
This candy costs fifty cents.
I have only ten cents in my pocket.
Milk is ninety-nine cents today.
There are a hundred cents in a dollar.
Talk to the management.
The management is new.
I study business management.
Management is on the third floor.
note: Management is uncountable: "the management", not "a management".

examples: I really like the design of your website.
The new phone has a nice design.
She studies fashion design at college.
The design of this kitchen is very simple.
My son is afraid of monsters.
There's no monster under your bed.
We watched a film about a sea monster.
The kids drew a funny green monster.
I'll send you an email tonight.
What is your email address?
I check my email every morning.
Thanks for your email.
You are making good progress in English.
The doctor is happy with my progress.
We made a lot of progress today.
How is the progress on the new house?
note: Uncountable: say "good progress," not "a progress" or "progresses."

meaning_hint: Only the noun (an official visit, a visit to the doctor); to visit is відвідувати.
examples: Thanks for your visit!
This is my first visit to New York.
My parents came for a short visit.
I have a visit to the doctor today.

meaning_hint: Mostly about American/foreign police; a Ukrainian police officer is поліцейський.
examples: The cop stopped me for speeding.
Call the cops!
Her brother is a cop in Chicago.
Two cops arrived at the scene.
note: Informal; "police officer" is more polite.

examples: We have a friendly community in our town.
The online community helped me fix my phone.
Our community has a big park.
She works at the community center.
Thanks a lot, bro!
Hey bro, what's up?
Bro, you're the best!
See you later, bro.
note: Very informal slang. Use only with close friends.

examples: The mayor opened the new park.
Who is the mayor of your city?
We voted for a new mayor.
The mayor spoke to the people.
She is the national tennis champion.
Our team became the champion this year.
He was the world champion in boxing.
The champion got a big gold cup.
There is no signal in this room.
My phone has a weak signal here.
I lost the signal in the tunnel.
Can you hear me? The signal is bad.

meaning_hint: Also a quota; the mathematical limit is границя.
examples: The speed limit here is 30 miles per hour.
There is a limit of two bags per person.
I have a limit on my credit card.
Is there an age limit for this ride?
That's bullshit, and you know it.
I don't believe his bullshit.
Stop telling me bullshit!
This story sounds like bullshit.
note: Very rude slang; don't use it at work or with strangers. Polite: nonsense.

examples: Water is an important natural resource.
This website is a great resource for students.
Our school has few resources for sports.
We need more resources to finish the project.
The media talked about the story all week.
My son spends hours on social media.
She works in the media.
Don't believe everything in the media.
note: Usually used with "the": the media. Social media = websites like online networks.

meaning_hint: In English mom (US) / mum (UK) is more usual; mama is childish or old-fashioned.
examples: The baby said "mama" for the first time.
Mama, can I have some milk?
She called her mama every Sunday.
Mama cooked dinner for everyone.
note: Informal or childish; "mom" is more common in American English.

meaning_hint: Mainly a mouse click; a clicking sound = клацання.
examples: One click and the file is open.
Buy this with just one click.
I heard a click and the door opened.
The site counts every click.
note: As a verb, "click" is more common: "Click the button."

meaning_hint: Shopping as a leisure activity; buying things in general is покупки.
examples: Let's go shopping on Saturday.
I do the shopping every Monday.
She loves shopping for shoes.
We went shopping at the mall.
note: Uncountable. Say "go shopping" or "do the shopping."

meaning_hint: Also written веб-сайт (older spelling); often just сайт.
examples: Visit our website.
The website is new.
I buy tickets on the website.
What is the website?

meaning_hint: Mainly a bank loan or buying on credit; English says take out a loan, not 'a credit'. Film credits = титри.
examples: We bought the car on credit.
The bank gave us credit for the house.
Can I buy this phone on credit?
I have no credit left on my card.
note: "Credit" is uncountable here. For money you borrow from a bank, "loan" is common.

examples: The police are looking into the incident.
There was an incident on the bus today.
Please report any incident to the manager.
Nobody was hurt in the incident.
note: Formal word. In everyday talk, people often say "something happened."

meaning_hint: In Ukrainian usually an office worker (often ironic: офісний клерк).
examples: Ask the clerk at the hotel desk.
The clerk gave me my change.
She works as a clerk in a bank.
The store clerk helped me find a shirt.

meaning_hint: Also a degree: кандидат наук ≈ PhD
examples: There are three candidates for the job.
Which candidate will you vote for?
She is the best candidate for this job.
The candidates talked on TV last night.
Check the status of your order online.
What is your relationship status?
I changed my status on the app.
The flight status says "delayed."
I forgot the password to my account.
Do you have an account on this site?
Log in to your account to see your orders.
I made a new email account.
note: Also means a bank account.

meaning_hint: British spelling: theatre.
examples: We went to the theater on Saturday.
The theater is next to the park.
I love the theater more than movies.
Our seats in the theater were great.
note: British spelling: theatre. In the US, "movie theater" is a cinema.

examples: Who is the author?
She is my favorite author.
The author is here today.
I like this author.
She won first prize in the contest.
The prize is a new bike.
What is the prize for the winner?
He got a prize for his photo.
Can I get you a cold drink?
She ordered a drink at the bar.
We went out for a drink after work.
Soft drinks are cheaper at the supermarket.

meaning_hint: A bar for drinks (also the unit of pressure); a metal bar is брусок, a chocolate bar is плитка.
examples: Let's meet at the bar after work.
The bar closes at midnight.
We had a drink at a small bar.
Is there a good bar near here?

meaning_hint: Male cousin only (female: кузина); the everyday word is двоюрідний брат.
examples: My cousin lives in Chicago.
I have ten cousins on my mom's side.
We visited our cousins for the holidays.
Her cousin is coming to the wedding.
note: Used for both male and female cousins.

examples: The senator answered our questions.
She wants to be a senator one day.
We wrote a letter to our senator.
The senator visited our school.
It often rains in this region.
This region is famous for its wine.
We traveled around the region by car.
Which region of the country are you from?

meaning_hint: Ukrainian фешн is mostly used in compounds (фешн-індустрія); the general word is мода.
examples: She loves fashion and new clothes.
Long coats are in fashion this year.
He works in the fashion business.
I don't follow fashion.

meaning_hint: концепт is used in design and science (концепт-кар = concept car); everyday 'concept' is often поняття.
examples: The concept is very easy to understand.
I like the concept of this café.
Time is a hard concept for small kids.
Can you explain the concept again?
The health inspector visited the restaurant.
A police inspector came to the house.
The inspector checked the building for safety.
The bus inspector asked to see my ticket.
She works as a TV reporter.
A reporter asked me some questions.
The reporters waited outside the building.
He wants to be a sports reporter.
We went to a music festival last summer.
The town has a food festival in May.
Tickets for the festival are sold out.
The festival lasts three days.

meaning_hint: In Ukrainian mostly a panel of judges at a competition; a court jury is usually присяжні.
examples: The jury liked her song best.
The jury chose the winner.
She was on the jury at the film festival.
The jury gave him first place.
note: Most often means people who decide a case in a court.

meaning_hint: In Ukrainian also a concerto.
examples: We have tickets for a concert tonight.
The concert starts at eight.
Did you enjoy the concert?
I went to my first concert at sixteen.
I don't drink alcohol.
No alcohol is allowed in the park.
Alcohol is bad for your health.
This drink has no alcohol.
note: Uncountable: no "an" and no plural.

examples: We are on a tight budget this month.
What is your budget for the trip?
This hotel is good for a small budget.
I made a budget for food and rent.
Let's order a pizza for dinner.
I'd like two slices of pizza, please.
We made homemade pizza with cheese and mushrooms.
This pizza place delivers until midnight.

meaning_hint: in Ukrainian used mostly for foreign women or jokingly
examples: Excuse me, madam, can I help you?
"This way, madam," said the waiter.
Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to you.
Good evening, madam.
note: Formal; "ma'am" is more common in American speech.

meaning_hint: Indeclinable in Ukrainian.
examples: She looked sexy in that red dress.
He thinks his new car is sexy.
The singer has a sexy voice.
That's a very sexy photo.
note: Informal; can sound rude when said about someone you don't know well.

meaning_hint: American English usually says sports (I like sports).
examples: What is your favorite sport?
I don't play any sports.
Soccer is a popular sport here.
My son does a lot of sports at school.
note: Americans usually say "sports": "Do you like sports?"

examples: We saw a tiger at the zoo.
The tiger is sleeping in the sun.
Tigers are big and strong.
My son drew a tiger at school.
I'd like chicken with rice, please.
We eat rice almost every day.
Can you cook the rice for dinner?
This rice is too salty.
note: Uncountable: some rice, not "a rice" or "rices".

examples: We visited an old palace in the city.
The king lived in this palace.
The palace has a beautiful garden.
Can we take photos inside the palace?

meaning_hint: Also used for 'phone number'.
examples: The telephone rang in the middle of the night.
She answered the telephone in the kitchen.
We spoke on the telephone for an hour.
Please write your telephone number here.
note: In everyday speech people usually just say "phone".

meaning_hint: Rare, a bit ironic; the usual word is відвідувач.
examples: We had visitors last weekend.
Visitors must sign in at the front desk.
The museum gets many visitors in summer.
Visitors can park here for free.
The farmer sells eggs at the market.
My grandfather was a farmer.
Farmers work very hard.
We buy milk from a local farmer.

meaning_hint: A social-media post or a position (guard post, job); mail is пошта, a pole is стовп.
examples: I liked your post about the trip.
Her last post got a lot of likes.
I wrote a short post on my blog.
Did you see his post this morning?

meaning_hint: In maths a factor (of multiplication) is usually множник
examples: Price is an important factor for me.
Weather is a big factor in our plans.
Stress is a factor in many illnesses.
Location was the main factor in our choice.
The alarm went off at six.
Someone set off the fire alarm.
I forgot to turn off the car alarm.
The alarm woke up the whole house.

meaning_hint: Only a sports match; a matchstick is сірник.
examples: Did you watch the match last night?
Our team won the match.
The tennis match lasted three hours.
Let's go to the soccer match on Sunday.
note: In the US, "game" is more common for team sports.
